keyframe_review.note: unverified: page budget. New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Racibórz row after 1304 although the duchy lasted to 1521. The page names its centres after 1281 (Wodzisław, Żory, Rybnik, Mikołów and Pszczyna under Przemysław) but no boundary or change of extent; dynasty change in 1337 (Opava Přemyslids), Bohemian fief from 1327.

ledger.note: 1281: the Duchy of Racibórz is split off Opole again. The page has the duchy split from Opole, along with Cieszyn and Bytom, after Władysław's death; infobox 'Split off Opole: 1281'. Mieszko and Przemysław rule it jointly. (The duchy first existed 1172-1202; see notes.)

union.text: Oświęcim, the former Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała River

region.text: Cieszyn and the former Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała River

ledger.note: 1290: Mieszko takes Cieszyn and Oświęcim out of Racibórz to found the Duchy of Cieszyn. 'After another partition in 1290, Mieszko took his residence in Cieszyn and became the first Duke of Teschen'; the Racibórz page says the duchy 'was recreated again, assigned to' Przemysław in 1290.

1336-1337: the Piast line ends and the duchy passes to the Přemyslid dukes of Opava. After Leszek died without issue (1336) King John of Bohemia seized the duchy and granted it to Nicholas II of Opava (infobox 'To the Přemyslid dukes of Opava: 1337'). Treated as a dynasty change within the same state.
1521: the Duchy of Racibórz is united with the Duchy of Opole under Jan II the Good (infobox 'United with Opole: 1521').
1521: end of the Duchy of Racibórz as a separate duchy, united with Opole; after Jan II's death in 1532 Opole and Racibórz fell to Bohemia (infobox 'Fell to Bohemia: 1532').

certainty.note: Neither page opened gives a treaty or survey line; the duchy is a set of named centres (Racibórz, Wodzisław, Żory, Rybnik, Mikołów, Pszczyna) and the Cieszyn and Oświęcim cut-outs are circles.

notes: Duchy of Racibórz, eu-15-i, 2 pages (budget 1-2). (1) Start 1281: the Racibórz page dates an earlier duchy 1172-1202 ('formed in 1172 as a territory for Mieszko'); it was united with Opole in 1202 and split off again in 1281. Cliopatria's Duchy of Opole row (1177-1304) carries 1202-1281, so the dossier starts at the re-creation; the Opole dossier of the other part should note the 1172-1202 separate duchy. (2) Cliopatria's Racibórz shape (3,384 km2, 1285-1304) still contains Cieszyn and Oświęcim after 1290: corrected by cutting two 25 km discs; the Duchy of Cieszyn (1290-1653) needs its own dossier, Cliopatria lacks it. (3) Vassalage: infobox 'Vassalized by Bohemia: 1327'; Leszek 'paid homage to King John of Bohemia' and the duchy became a Bohemian fief. This is a vassal_start for counterpart duchy-of-raciborz that belongs in the kingdom-of-bohemia ledger (other agent). The Cieszyn page dates a 1291 agreement of Mieszko and Bolko I of Opole with Wenceslaus II; the Racibórz page does not say whether Przemysław took part in 1289-1292, so no earlier vassalage is recorded. (4) 1305-1520 is carried forward from the corrected 1294 shape (Cliopatria stops in 1304; unverified: page budget); 1337 is a dynasty change (rename). Dukes in 1337-1424 are listed from the page (Nicholas II 1337-1365 and so on); Nicholas II of Opava is the Opava Přemyslid. (5) Pages disagree on Mieszko's rule: the ruler list gives 1281-1290 joint, the Cieszyn page makes him duke of Teschen from 1290. (6) No war: neither page names a war of the duchy; no Hungary or Kraków border event is on these pages although Cliopatria lists Kingdom of Hungary and Grand Duchy of Kraków as neighbours 1285-1304. (7) No infobox area on any page opened. (8) Gazetteer names needed: Racibórz, Cieszyn, Oświęcim, Wodzisław, Żory, Rybnik (places; Racibórz c. 18.22 E 50.09 N, Cieszyn c. 18.63 E 49.75 N, Oświęcim c. 19.22 E 50.04 N).
